description: BATADAL provides the datasets of the Battle of the Attack Detection Algorithms, a competition on detecting cyber-physical attacks against water distribution networks. The data are hourly historical SCADA operations of C-Town, a benchmark network, generated by simulation: training dataset 1 (released 20 November 2016) is a one-year record of normal operation without attacks; training dataset 2 (28 November 2016) covers about six months and contains several attacks, some approximately labelled; the test dataset (20 February 2017) covers three months with unlabelled attacks and was used to rank the entries. Flows are in litres per second and pressures and water levels in metres; lists of the attacks and the C-Town EPANET input file are provided. An international group of water and security researchers organised it and reported the results in the Journal of Water Resources Planning and Management in August 2018 (Taormina et al.), which users are asked to cite. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC-BY-4.0. Access is free of charge. The network is synthetic, so coverage is the benchmark, not a real utility. Caveats: two earlier datasets were withdrawn as obsolete because their demand patterns differed from the test data, and the attack scenarios are simulated, not observed. Simulation uses: testing anomaly and attack detection for water digital twins, resilience and emergency response to cyber attacks. Related records: EPANET (model-epanet) and LeakDB (data-leakdb).
